HEALTHY, reported metrics were misleading due to a real bug (now fixed) (first trial on the new 383-coarse-GO-term task: val_loss improves cleanly 0.0803->0.0772 over 10 epochs, best at epoch 7. Training-loop val_recall (2.7-3.6% the whole run) looked like a collapse, but a proper diagnostic (experiments/scripts/diagnostic_eval_stage2.py) on the same checkpoint found median per-label AUROC=0.84, pooled precision/recall/F1@0.5=0.66/0.46/0.54 - a genuinely well-performing model. Root cause: compute_metrics() averaged per-batch recall ratios (batch_size=8, 383 sparse labels at 3.58% positive means most (label,batch) pairs have zero true positives, so tp/(tp+fn+eps)=0 dominates the batch average regardless of model quality) instead of pooling tp/fn across the whole epoch first. Fixed in training_run.py (compute_metrics()/finalize_metrics() now accumulate raw counts and compute the ratio once) - confirmed via a synthetic test: a model with true recall=1.0 was reported as 25.7% recall under the old code, 100% under the fix. Every prior trial's accuracy was unaffected by this bug (only recall's ratio-averaging was wrong); recall numbers on prior 3-label trials were only mildly affected since 3 labels rarely hit zero-positives-per-batch the way 383 labels do)

NEGATIVE RESULT for pos_weight as tried (isolated A/B vs trial-050, only --pos-weight added: sqrt(n_neg/n_pos) per label). val_loss/recall from the training log are NOT directly comparable to trial-050's - pos_weight changes the loss function's numeric scale (up to 69x on rare-label positives) and trial-050's own recall was computed under the old buggy metric, so a proper diagnostic (experiments/scripts/diagnostic_eval_stage2.py) was run on both checkpoints for an apples-to-apples read. Result: median per-label AUROC ticked up slightly (0.8456 vs 0.8366) and the optimal threshold recalibrated back toward 0.5 as intended (0.48 vs trial-050's 0.32) - pos_weight's mechanism works - but best-achievable pooled F1 got WORSE (0.5007 vs 0.5727): at threshold 0.5, recall rose (45.8%->52.9%) but precision fell harder (65.7%->47.2%), a net-negative trade. sqrt(n_neg/n_pos) as formulated overcorrects for this dataset; a gentler compression (e.g. ratio**0.3) or no pos_weight (just post-hoc threshold tuning, which is free and doesn't disturb the trained representation) may be the better direction
